items.title: [Server] Stop the stdio server from answering a notification it refuses

items.title: [Server] Add `Psr6SessionStore` and `Psr6NotificationBus`
items.excerpt: As discussed in https://github.com/symfony/ai/issues/2853: the Symfony MCP Bundle wraps `cache.app`, a PSR-6 pool, in `Psr16Cache` to use `Psr16SessionStore` and `Psr16NotificationBus`. items.title: [Server] Fix stdio server ending by itself on an idle Windows pipe

It also turns control characters into `_`, so `http://evil.example .localhost` passes as well. None of these characters are valid in a URL, so `SecureUrl` refuses them now. When a request's fiber is dropped while it waits for the server, e.g. a `2026-07-28` handler asked the client for input and the `input_required` answer ended the request, and the handler throws while it unwinds (in a `finally`), `HandlerFiberState::threw()` kept the throwable for a rethrow that never comes: the failure was lost without a trace. `HandlerFibers::step()` now marks the state while the

items.title: [Server] Read only new entries when polling `InMemoryNotificationBus`
items.excerpt: `InMemoryNotificationBus::since()` walked its whole backlog on every poll, so each caught-up `subscriptions/listen` stream paid for every entry kept. Sequences have no gaps, so it now reads from the cursor only, and hands the backlog back in one go to a reader that fell behind it. On PHP 8.5, a caught-up poll drops from 2.9 µs to 0.07 µs with the default backlog of 256, and from 114 µs to 0.07 µs with 10,000 entries.

items.title: [Server] Give `FileSessionStore` a time budget for replacing a held session file on Windows
items.excerpt: Follow-up to #702 and #717. On Windows, `rename()` can't replace a file anyone has open, readers included. Under the concurrent writer test the target stayed held for up to ~240 ms, longer than the 10 attempts covered. items.title: [Server] Fix variadic enum parameters declaring their items as objects
items.excerpt: A variadic enum parameter like `Color ...$colors` was advertised as `{"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object"}}`, so `{"colors": ["red", "blue"]}` got `-32602 Expected object, but received string` and no input could reach the handler. The items now list the enum's values, like for a single enum parameter, so the call validates and the handler gets the enum cases. Found, fixed and written up with Claude Code.

items.title: [Server] Fix iterable parameters being declared as objects
items.excerpt: An `iterable $items` parameter was advertised as `{"type": "object"}`, so `{"items": [1, 2]}` got `-32602 Expected object, but received array`, although `iterable ` already maps to `array` and the argument is cast like an `array` one. It now gets `{"type": "array"}`, which means a JSON object is refused instead, as for `array`, hence the `[BC Break]` entry. Found, fixed and written up with Claude Code.
